title: Go: TCP Server and Chat Relay
description: Build a TCP server from scratch with concurrent connection handling and a simple chat relay system.

steps.title: Listen for TCP connections
steps.description: Use `net.Listen("tcp", ":9000")` to start a TCP listener. Print the listener address with `fmt.Printf("Listening on %s\n", listener.Addr())`. Accept exactly one connection with `listener.Accept()` and print the remote address using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Accept blocks until a connection arrives

verification.successMessage: TCP listener created and accepted a connection!
verification.failureMessage: Print the listener address and remote address.

steps.title: Handle connection in a goroutine
steps.description: Wrap connection handling in `go handleConn(conn net.Conn)`. Inside, set a read deadline with `conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(30*time.Second))` and use a `for` loop with a buffered reader (`bufio.NewReader`) to read line-delimited messages using `reader.ReadString('\n')`. Print each message.
hints: Each connection gets its own goroutine
bufio.NewReader wraps the connection for line reading
Read deadline prevents hanging on idle connections

verification.failureMessage: Print each received message and its sender.

steps.title: Write back to the connection
steps.description: Echo received messages back to the sender using `fmt.Fprintf(conn, "Echo: %s", message)`. Add a welcome message sent on connect. Print sent data using `fmt.Printf("Sent: %s", ...)`.
hints: fmt.Fprintf writes formatted strings to a writer
Send welcome message immediately after Accept

verification.failureMessage: Print the echo response being sent.

steps.title: Chat relay: broadcast hub
steps.description: Create a `Hub` struct with a `clients map[net.Conn]string` (conn → name) and a `broadcast chan string`. A `Run()` goroutine reads from the broadcast channel and writes to all connected clients. Print broadcast messages using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Hub.Run() is a single goroutine that serializes all writes
Use a map to track all connected clients
Remove clients that fail to write (broken pipe)

verification.failureMessage: Print broadcast messages being relayed to clients.

steps.title: Client connect/disconnect lifecycle
steps.description: Enhance `handleConn` to register with the Hub on connect (send "joined" message) and unregister on disconnect with `defer`. Close the connection and broadcast "left" message. Print join/leave events using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Use a unique name like fmt.Sprintf("User-%d", id)

verification.failureMessage: Print join and leave events for each client.

steps.title: Graceful TCP server shutdown
steps.description: Add a `Shutdown()` method to the server that closes the listener (preventing new connections), signals all handlers with a context, and waits for active connections to finish using `sync.WaitGroup`. Print shutdown status using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Pass context to handleConn for cancellation

verification.failureMessage: Print shutdown progress for listener and connections.
